rejected_hypotheses.reason: violates temporal order rule: vendor degradation notice posted after internal errors started (E4), and no evidence of vendor degradation before error spike (E3).
violates counterfactual rule 2: error growth stopped immediately after rollback started (E2), treating rollback as irrelevant is invalid.

conflict_chain: Three candidate explanations compete: hyp_a (parser regression), hyp_b (vendor outage), hyp_c (unrelated background condition).
Applying counterfactual rules: hyp_b rejected due to temporal order violation (trigger after onset); hyp_c rejected due to ignoring rollback-correlated recovery.
Only hyp_a survives: it directly explains earliest initiating signal (new parser enabled before error spike) and matches rollback stopping error growth.
governing_rule: If multiple hypotheses survive, prefer the one that directly explains the earliest initiating signal.
